This report was rendered on `r format(Sys.time(), "%B %d, %Y")`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, dev = "png", dpi = 150)
```

```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

# corrected data (manual corrections pending confirmation by curators)
dat <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds")

# one row per study: metadata are shared by the increased and decreased signatures
studies <- dat |>
  distinct(Study, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, -`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, -`Abundance in Group 1`) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

# colors: health/periodontitis, periodontitis classification, profiling method
# (method colors match the overview figure of the main report; grey is always "not reported")
pal_group <- c(Health = "#2a78d6", Periodontitis = "#eb6834")

class_levels <- c(
  "Chronic periodontitis", "Chronic and aggressive periodontitis", "Aggressive periodontitis",
  "Periodontitis (stage/grade)", "Refractory periodontitis", "Periodontitis (type not specified)"
)
class_short <- c("Chronic", "Chronic + aggressive", "Aggressive", "Stage/grade", "Refractory", "Not specified")
pal_class <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6", "#e87ba4", "#eda100", "#e34948", "grey65"), class_short)

method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                   "PCR", "Other / not reported")
pal_method <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65"), method_levels)

theme_meta <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
theme_set(theme_meta)

studies <- studies |>
  mutate(
    classification = factor(
      class_short[match(`Periodontitis classification`, class_levels)], levels = class_short
    ),
    method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    ) |> factor(levels = method_levels),
    period = cut(Year, c(-Inf, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                 labels = c("1995–2004", "2005–2009", "2010–2014", "2015–2019", "2020–2025"))
  )

# group-level measures in long format
features <- tribble(
  ~feature,   ~label,                          ~mean_col,                        ~sd_col,
  "age",      "Age (years)",                   "age mean",                       "age sd",
  "males",    "Males (%)",                     "percent males",                  NA,
  "smokers",  "Smokers (%)",                   "percent smokers",                NA,
  "pd",       "Probing depth (mm)",            "pocket depth mean (mm)",         "pocket depth sd",
  "cal",      "Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "clinical attachment loss (mm)",  "clinical attachment loss sd",
  "bop",      "Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "bleeding on probing percent",    "bleeding on probing sd",
  "plaque",   "Plaque (% sites)",              "plaque",                         "plaque sd",
  "supp",     "Suppuration (% sites)",         "suppuration percent",            "suppuration sd"
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

long <- pmap_dfr(features, function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
  map_dfr(0:1, function(g) {
    col <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) NA_real_ else studies[[paste("Group", g, x)]]
    num <- if (feature %in% c("males", "smokers")) col(paste("num", feature)) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      Study = studies$Study, feature = feature, label = label,
      group = c("Health", "Periodontitis")[g + 1],
      mean = col(mean_col), sd = col(sd_col),
      n = studies[[paste("Group", g, "sample size")]],
      num = num
    )
  })
}) |>
  # plaque indices (e.g. Silness-Löe 0-3) are not comparable with % sites
  left_join(select(studies, Study, `Plaque measure`), by = "Study") |>
  filter(!is.na(mean), feature != "plaque" | `Plaque measure` %in% "% sites") |>
  select(-`Plaque measure`)

# studies with values for both groups
paired <- long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Study, feature, label), names_from = group,
              values_from = c(mean, sd, n, num)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_Health), !is.na(mean_Periodontitis)) |>
  # smokers excluded from both groups: no contrast
  filter(!(feature == "smokers" & mean_Health == 0 & mean_Periodontitis == 0))

paired_tests <- paired |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    p = wilcox.test(mean_Periodontitis, mean_Health, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", signif(p, 2))))
```

## About this report

This report sets out candidate figures and tables on the metadata of PerioSigDB. It covers how participant and clinical characteristics differ between periodontitis and periodontally healthy groups, and how they vary across studies. Each section is one option, with a short note on what it shows and its caveats. A summary of all options with a recommendation is at the end.

All analyses use the **corrected** dataset (`output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds`). Its manual corrections are pending confirmation by the curators; see `output/manual_corrections.csv`. The unit of analysis is the **study** (n = `r nrow(studies)`), because metadata are recorded once per study and shared by its increased and decreased signatures. Group 0 is the periodontally healthy group and Group 1 the periodontitis group. Health groups are not uniform:

- Studies 298, 153 and 155 include gingivitis subjects in Group 0.
- Studies 1752, 1818 and 1897 use periodontitis-resistant adults aged 65 and over.

# Data availability

## Option 1: Metadata completeness heatmap

```{r completeness}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Reporting of metadata across studies. Each column is a study, ordered by publication year; each row is a field. Group-level fields are shaded by whether they are reported for both groups, one group, or neither. Plaque counts as reported only when given as % of sites. Non-healthy systemic condition is shaded only for studies whose participants have a systemic condition (e.g. diabetes). The percentage after each field is the share of studies reporting it for both groups (group-level fields) or at all (study-level fields)."

study_fields <- tibble(
  Study = studies$Study,
  `Profiling method` = studies$method != "Other / not reported",
  `16S variable region` = !is.na(studies$`16S variable region`),
  `Periodontitis classification` = studies$classification != "Not specified",
  `Non-healthy systemic condition` = !is.na(studies$`Systemic condition`) &
    studies$`Systemic condition` != "systemically healthy",
  `Group 0 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 0 definition`),
  `Group 1 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 1 definition`)
) |>
  pivot_longer(-Study, names_to = "field", values_to = "reported") |>
  mutate(status = ifelse(reported, "Reported", "Not reported"), type = "Study")

size_fields <- studies |>
  transmute(Study, n0 = !is.na(`Group 0 sample size`), n1 = !is.na(`Group 1 sample size`)) |>
  mutate(field = "Sample size")

group_fields <- long |>
  distinct(Study, label, group) |>
  count(Study, field = as.character(label), name = "groups") |>
  complete(Study = studies$Study, field = levels(features$label), fill = list(groups = 0)) |>
  bind_rows(transmute(size_fields, Study, field, groups = n0 + n1)) |>
  mutate(
    status = c("Neither group", "One group", "Both groups")[groups + 1],
    type = "Group"
  )

completeness <- bind_rows(group_fields, study_fields) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(
    Study = fct_reorder(Study, Year, .fun = min),
    complete = status %in% c("Both groups", "Reported")
  ) |>
  mutate(field_label = paste0(field, " (", round(100 * mean(complete)), "%)"), .by = field)

field_order <- completeness |>
  summarise(pct = mean(complete), type = first(type), .by = field_label) |>
  arrange(type == "Study", pct) |>
  pull(field_label)

pal_status <- c(
  "Both groups" = "#2a78d6", "One group" = "#9ec5f4", "Neither group" = "#f0efec",
  "Reported" = "#256abf", "Not reported" = "#f0efec"
)

ggplot(completeness, aes(x = Study, y = factor(field_label, levels = field_order), fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_status, breaks = c("Both groups", "One group", "Neither group")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = NULL, breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Studies (ordered by publication year →)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank())
```

**Shows:** how complete each field is, and whether reporting improved over time. For example, recent studies more often give a periodontitis stage/grade. This is useful as a supplementary figure in a resource paper, and it sets expectations for every other option below.

**Caveat:** "Not reported" can also mean "not entered". Systemic condition was not extracted for most studies in the original overview sheet, so studies with comorbid participants may be missed.

# Health vs periodontitis

## Option 2: Paired study-level comparison

```{r paired-slopes}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Health vs periodontitis within each study. Grey lines join the two groups of one study; large points are medians across studies. n is the number of studies reporting the measure for both groups; p is from a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies."

medians <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(label, group))

strip_labels <- paired_tests |>
  arrange(label) |>
  mutate(strip = paste0(label, "\nn = ", studies, ", ", p_label)) |>
  mutate(strip = factor(strip, levels = strip)) |>
  select(label, strip)

long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  left_join(strip_labels, by = "label") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
            aes(y = median, group = 1), color = "grey15", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
             aes(y = median, fill = group), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 4, stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~strip, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**Shows:** the size and consistency of the health–periodontitis difference for each measure, and how much individual studies vary around it. Clinical measures separate almost every study. The demographic measures show the imbalances between groups: periodontitis groups tend to be older and to smoke more.

**Caveat:** each study counts equally, regardless of its sample size.

## Option 3: Disease severity by periodontitis classification

```{r within-perio}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values across studies, by periodontitis classification (one point per study). Bars are medians. Smokers at 0% are mostly studies that excluded smokers."

within <- long |>
  filter(group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("age", "smokers", "pd", "cal", "bop")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, classification), by = "Study")

ggplot(within, aes(x = classification, y = mean, color = classification)) +
  geom_quasirandom(size = 1.8, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey15") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_class) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

**Shows:** whether "periodontitis" means comparable disease across studies. Aggressive-periodontitis studies are younger and have deeper pockets, while unspecified and stage/grade studies span a wide severity range.

**Caveat:** some groups have few studies (e.g. refractory n = 1). PD/CAL are sometimes from sampled sites only, which inflates them.

## Option 4: Trends over publication year

```{r trends}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values by publication year (one point per study). Black lines are linear trends with 95% confidence bands."

within |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = mean)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "grey60", color = "white", size = 2.4, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "grey10", fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = NULL)
```

**Shows:** whether the periodontitis cohorts recruited have changed over three decades of publications (e.g. older patients and higher BOP in recent studies). This is relevant to whether older and newer signatures are comparable.

**Caveat:** publication year is confounded with profiling method, since sequencing replaced hybridization and PCR over the same period, so a time trend cannot be separated from a method effect.

# Study characteristics

## Option 5: Periodontitis classification over time and by method

```{r classification}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Periodontitis classification of studies by publication period (share of studies; counts in bars). (B) Number of studies by classification and profiling method."

pA <- studies |>
  count(period, classification) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), .by = period) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = fct_rev(period), fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop > 0.06, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            color = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

pB <- studies |>
  count(classification, method) |>
  complete(classification, method, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = fct_rev(classification), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, ""), color = n > 12), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab", guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
```

**Shows:** the shift from the 1999 chronic/aggressive classification to the 2018 stage/grade system, and which diagnosis types each profiling method has studied. This is useful context for stratifying signatures.

**Caveat:** "Not specified" is large. Many older studies define periodontitis only by PD/CAL thresholds.

## Option 6: Systemic condition of participants

```{r systemic}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Systemic condition of participants (number of studies). Not recorded: not extracted in the overview sheet."

studies |>
  mutate(systemic = case_when(
    is.na(`Systemic condition`) ~ "Not recorded",
    `Systemic condition` == "systemically healthy" ~ "Systemically healthy",
    .default = str_to_sentence(`Systemic condition`)
  )) |>
  count(systemic) |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      systemic == "Not recorded" ~ "Not recorded",
      systemic == "Systemically healthy" ~ "Systemically healthy",
      .default = "Includes systemic disease"
    ),
    systemic = fct_reorder(systemic, n)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = systemic, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Systemically healthy" = "#2a78d6", "Includes systemic disease" = "#eb6834",
                               "Not recorded" = "grey65")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL)
```

**Shows:** which signatures come from populations with comorbidities (rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, COPD, HIV), so they can be flagged or excluded in sensitivity analyses.

**Caveat:** this is unknown for about half the studies until the curators fill it in. It might work better as a table than a figure.

# Comparison with BugSigDB

```{r bugsigdb-load}
# BugSigDB export (cached by bugsigdbr; version date from its message)
bsdb_version <- NA_character_
bsdb <- withCallingHandlers(
  bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB(),
  warning = function(w) {
    bsdb_version <<- sub(".*from ", "", conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
if (is.na(bsdb_version)) bsdb_version <- format(Sys.Date())

oral_sites <- "plaque|saliva|mouth|oral|tongue|gingiv|throat|oroph|tonsil|buccal|cheek"

# BugSigDB without its periodontitis signatures (PerioSigDB is the reference for those)
bsdb_other <- filter(bsdb, !grepl("periodont", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE))

db_levels <- c("PerioSigDB", "BugSigDB")
pal_db <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6"), db_levels)

# genera of the taxa in a signature (taxa above genus rank are dropped)
genera <- function(x) unique(sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", x[grepl("g__", x)]))

sig_genera <- function(d) {
  tibble(
    sig = seq_len(nrow(d)), Condition = d$Condition, `Body site` = d$`Body site`,
    direction = d$`Abundance in Group 1`, taxon = map(d$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)
  ) |>
    unnest(taxon)
}
```

PerioSigDB uses BugSigDB's format, so its signatures can be set against the rest of the microbiome literature. These options use the BugSigDB export of `r bsdb_version`, with `r n_distinct(bsdb$PMID)` studies and `r nrow(bsdb)` signatures across all conditions and body sites. BugSigDB's own periodontitis signatures (`r nrow(bsdb) - nrow(bsdb_other)`) are excluded throughout.

## Option 7: Profiling methods and taxonomic resolution

```{r bsdb-methods}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "(A) Profiling method of signatures. (B) Taxonomic rank of the taxa in signatures. BugSigDB includes all conditions and body sites except periodontitis."

method_of <- function(type, platform) {
  case_when(
    type == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
    type == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
    type %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
    platform == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
    .default = "Other / not reported"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)
}

methods_db <- bind_rows(
  dat |> transmute(db = "PerioSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`)),
  bsdb_other |> transmute(db = "BugSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`))
) |>
  count(db, method) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

rank_names <- c(s = "Species", g = "Genus", f = "Family", o = "Order", c = "Class", p = "Phylum", k = "Kingdom")
pal_rank <- c(Species = "#184f95", Genus = "#3987e5", Family = "#86b6ef", Higher = "#cde2fb")

ranks_db <- bind_rows(
  tibble(db = "PerioSigDB", taxon = unlist(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`)),
  tibble(db = "BugSigDB", taxon = unlist(bsdb_other$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`))
) |>
  mutate(
    rank = rank_names[substr(sub(".*[|]", "", taxon), 1, 1)],
    rank = factor(ifelse(rank %in% c("Species", "Genus", "Family"), rank, "Higher"), levels = names(pal_rank))
  ) |>
  count(db, rank) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

stack_bar <- function(d, fill, pal, tag) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = db, fill = {{ fill }})) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.06, scales::percent(prop, 1), "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}

stack_bar(methods_db, method, pal_method, "A") +
  stack_bar(ranks_db, rank, pal_rank, "B") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```

**Shows:** PerioSigDB is dominated by targeted assays (checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization and PCR) that report named species, whereas BugSigDB is mostly 16S and shotgun sequencing reported at genus level. This is the main structural difference between the two databases. It is why Option 9 compares them at genus level.

## Option 8: Metadata captured by each database

```{r bsdb-fields}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Share of signatures with each field filled in, by database. BugSigDB records statistical methods and diversity; PerioSigDB records participant and clinical characteristics."

filled <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) return(lengths(x) > 0)
  !is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA"))
}
field_share <- function(d, db, fields) {
  tibble(
    db = db, field = fields,
    share = map_dbl(fields, \(f) if (f %in% names(d)) mean(filled(d[[f]])) else NA_real_)
  )
}

shared_fields <- c("Group 1 definition", "Group 0 sample size", "Group 1 sample size",
                   "Sequencing type", "16S variable region", "Sequencing platform", "Location of subjects")
bsdb_fields <- c("Statistical test", "Significance threshold", "MHT correction", "LDA Score above",
                 "Matched on", "Confounders controlled for", "Antibiotics exclusion", "Shannon", "Richness")
perio_fields <- c("Group 0 definition", "Periodontitis classification", "Systemic condition",
                  "Group 1 age mean", "Group 1 percent males", "Group 1 percent smokers",
                  "Group 1 pocket depth mean (mm)", "Group 1 clinical attachment loss (mm)",
                  "Group 1 bleeding on probing percent", "Group 1 plaque")
all_fields <- c(shared_fields, bsdb_fields, perio_fields)
field_label <- function(x) sub("^Group 0 ", "Health ", sub("^Group 1 ", "Periodontitis ", x))

fields_db <- bind_rows(
  field_share(dat, "PerioSigDB", all_fields),
  field_share(bsdb_other, "BugSigDB", all_fields)
) |>
  mutate(
    # classification "not specified" counts as missing
    share = ifelse(db == "PerioSigDB" & field == "Periodontitis classification",
                   mean(dat$`Periodontitis classification` != "Periodontitis (type not specified)"), share),
    field_type = case_when(
      field %in% shared_fields ~ "Both databases",
      field %in% bsdb_fields ~ "BugSigDB only",
      .default = "PerioSigDB only"
    ),
    field = factor(field_label(field), levels = rev(field_label(all_fields))),
    db = factor(db, levels = db_levels)
  )

ggplot(fields_db, aes(x = db, y = field)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = share, fill = db), shape = 21, color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(share), "–", scales::percent(share, 1))),
            nudge_x = 0.22, hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(field_type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_db, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.7))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

**Shows:** the two databases record complementary metadata. PerioSigDB adds participant and clinical characteristics that BugSigDB has no fields for. BugSigDB records the statistical test, significance threshold, multiple-testing correction and matching, which PerioSigDB lacks. Adding those fields to PerioSigDB would make it fully importable into BugSigDB.

**Caveats:**

- A filled field is not necessarily a complete one (e.g. "Matched on" can list only some of the variables).
- PerioSigDB's lower sequencing type completeness is mostly checkerboard hybridization, which has no sequencing type in BugSigDB's vocabulary.

## Option 9: PerioSigDB taxa across other conditions

```{r bsdb-conditions-data}
# genera with the most consistent direction in PerioSigDB: exact binomial test of increased vs
# decreased signatures against 50% (as for taxa in the main report), then how often the top 20
# in each direction appear in BugSigDB signatures of the same direction for each other condition
n_sig_dir <- table(dat$`Abundance in Group 1`)

perio_tests <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    signatures = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased")
  )

perio_genera <- perio_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20, by = direction) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05",
      p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05 (not FDR)",
      .default = "Not significant"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)", "Not significant"))
  )

# body site group of each signature (signatures listing sites in several groups are "mixed")
gi_sites <- paste0("feces|colon|colorectal|intestin|caecum|cecum|rectum|ileum|jejunum|duoden|stomach|",
                   "gastric|esophag|meconium|digestive|bile|rumen|cloaca|midgut|proventriculus")
site_group <- function(sites) {
  map_chr(strsplit(sites, ","), function(x) {
    groups <- unique(case_when(
      grepl(oral_sites, x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "oral",
      grepl(gi_sites, x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "gastrointestinal",
      .default = "other"
    ))
    if (length(groups) == 1) groups else "mixed"
  })
}

# disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only: Group 0 is a control group and Group 1 is not.
# This drops body site, time point, treatment arm, diet and reversed comparisons, which BugSigDB
# also files under the study's condition
control_names <- paste0("control|healthy|\\bhealth\\b|normal|\\bnon[- ]?|without|negative|unaffected|",
                        "\\bHC\\b|\\bNC\\b|cognitively (intact|unimpaired)|^no\\b|-free\\b|peritumo|adjacent|benign")
bsdb_cc <- bsdb_other |>
  filter(grepl(control_names, `Group 0 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl(control_names, `Group 1 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         `Abundance in Group 1` %in% c("increased", "decreased"))

# count each study once per condition, direction and body site group: the units below are
# study-level, and a genus is in a unit if it is in any of the study's signatures in that unit
bsdb_cc_sigs <- tibble(
  sig = seq_len(nrow(bsdb_cc)), bsdb_id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study,
  Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition, direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  oral = grepl(oral_sites, bsdb_cc$`Body site`, ignore.case = TRUE),
  site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`)
) |>
  mutate(unit = as.integer(factor(paste(Study, Condition, direction, site_group, sep = "|"))))

bsdb_sigs <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  summarise(oral = any(oral), .by = c(unit, Study, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  rename(sig = unit)

bsdb_genera <- sig_genera(bsdb_cc) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_cc_sigs, sig, unit), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(sig = unit, direction, taxon)

# left panel: PerioSigDB signatures with the genus increased (right) and decreased (left)
perio_panel <- function(top, genus_levels) {
  perio_counts <- top |>
    select(taxon, increased, decreased, significance) |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))

  max_n <- max(abs(perio_counts$n))
  ggplot(perio_counts, aes(x = n, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = significance), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = distinct(top, taxon, fdr),
              aes(x = -max_n * 1.05, label = ifelse(fdr < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", fdr))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.5, color = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = NULL) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                       drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = scales::breaks_extended()(c(-max_n, max_n)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures\n(left: FDR)", y = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 1), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1)) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}

# top bar: share of each column's signatures from oral body sites
oral_panel <- function(columns) {
  ggplot(columns, aes(x = col, y = oral)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 0.7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Oral sites") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}

# one-sided test of a genus being in a condition's signatures more often than in other conditions'
# signatures from the same body site group; strata without both are uninformative and dropped
site_matched_p <- function(condition, genus, sigs, hits) {
  d <- sigs |>
    mutate(in_condition = Condition == condition, has_genus = sig %in% hits$sig[hits$taxon == genus])
  informative <- d |>
    summarise(ok = any(in_condition) & any(!in_condition), .by = site_group) |>
    filter(ok) |>
    pull(site_group)
  if (!length(informative)) return(NA_real_)
  d <- filter(d, site_group %in% informative)
  tab <- table(factor(d$in_condition, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$has_genus, c(TRUE, FALSE)),
               factor(d$site_group))
  if (dim(tab)[3] == 1) {
    fisher.test(tab[, , 1], alternative = "greater")$p.value
  } else {
    mantelhaen.test(tab, exact = TRUE, alternative = "greater")$p.value
  }
}

# match_site = TRUE compares each condition with other signatures from the same body site group
# (exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site group) instead of all other signatures
condition_heatmap <- function(dir, n_conditions = 15, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)

  # enrichment of each genus in each condition's signatures vs all other BugSigDB signatures of
  # this direction: one-sided Fisher's exact test, BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
  condition_sizes <- sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)

  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")

  enrichment <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, taxon, name = "n") |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = condition_sizes$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(
      n = coalesce(n, 0L), with_genus = coalesce(with_genus, 0L),
      share = n / signatures,
      p = if (match_site) {
        map2_dbl(Condition, taxon, site_matched_p, sigs = sigs, hits = hits)
      } else {
        pmap_dbl(list(n, signatures, with_genus), function(a, n_cond, n_genus) {
          fisher.test(matrix(c(a, n_cond - a, n_genus - a, nrow(sigs) - n_cond - n_genus + a), 2),
                      alternative = "greater")$p.value
        })
      },
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )

  # conditions with the most significantly enriched genera (ties: smallest combined p-value)
  conditions <- enrichment |>
    summarise(n_enriched = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), score = sum(-log10(p), na.rm = TRUE),
              .by = c(Condition, signatures, oral)) |>
    arrange(desc(n_enriched), desc(score)) |>
    slice_head(n = n_conditions)

  # first column: all BugSigDB signatures of this direction (baseline)
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(sigs), oral = mean(sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  baseline <- tibble(taxon = top$taxon) |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    transmute(Condition = "All BugSigDB", taxon, share = coalesce(with_genus, 0L) / nrow(sigs), fdr = NA_real_)

  shares <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
    select(Condition, taxon, share, fdr) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05)

  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)
  high <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"

  p_heat <- ggplot(shares, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = share)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(shares, enriched), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(enriched | share >= 0.1, round(100 * share), ""),
                  color = share > 0.45, fontface = ifelse(enriched, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.7) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA),
                        name = "BugSigDB\nstudies") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey20", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         caption = if (match_site) {
           "Outlined, bold: enriched vs other studies from the same body site group (exact CMH test, FDR < 0.05)"
         } else {
           "Outlined, bold: enriched vs all other BugSigDB studies (Fisher's exact test, FDR < 0.05)"
         }) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it increased vs decreased against 50% (the same test as for PerioSigDB),
# BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
direction_heatmap <- function(dir, n_conditions = 15, min_sigs = 5) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)

  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon) |>
    left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, direction), by = "sig") |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased"))

  condition_sizes <- bsdb_sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)

  direction_test <- function(d) {
    d |>
      mutate(
        n = increased + decreased,
        same = if (dir == "increased") increased else decreased,
        share_same = same / n,
        p = map2_dbl(same, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
        fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
      )
  }
  count_directions <- function(d, ...) {
    d |>
      count(..., taxon, direction) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
      (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                    decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))()
  }

  tests <- hits |>
    filter(Condition %in% condition_sizes$Condition) |>
    count_directions(Condition) |>
    direction_test()

  baseline <- hits |>
    count_directions() |>
    direction_test() |>
    mutate(Condition = "All BugSigDB")

  # conditions with the most genera significantly in the same direction as periodontitis
  conditions <- tests |>
    summarise(n_consistent = sum(fdr < 0.05 & share_same > 0.5),
              score = sum(-log10(p[share_same > 0.5])), .by = Condition) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    arrange(desc(n_consistent), desc(score)) |>
    slice_head(n = n_conditions)

  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(bsdb_sigs), oral = mean(bsdb_sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  cells <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(tests, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = columns$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(
      significant = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
      # too few signatures to show a direction
      few = !is.na(n) & n < 3,
      share_plot = ifelse(few, NA, share_same),
      label = ifelse(!is.na(n) & !few, paste0(same, "/", n), "")
    )

  same_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"
  opposite_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#1c5cab" else "#c2410c"

  p_heat <- ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = share_plot)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, few), fill = "grey85", color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, significant), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.4, color = "grey15") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = opposite_col, mid = "#f0efec", high = same_col, midpoint = 0.5,
                         limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, na.value = "white",
                         name = paste0("Studies\nreporting it\n", dir)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         caption = paste0("Cell labels: studies with the genus ", dir, " / all studies with the genus.\n",
                          "Outlined, bold: binomial test FDR < 0.05. Grey: 1-2 studies. White: genus not reported.")) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}
```

Where else in the microbiome literature (BugSigDB) do the taxa that PerioSigDB links to periodontitis turn up? BugSigDB is restricted to disease-vs-control comparisons (`r nrow(bsdb_cc)` signatures from `r n_distinct(bsdb_cc$Study)` studies), and each study counts once per condition, direction and body site group.

The genus heatmaps use the 20 most significant PerioSigDB genera per direction (left panel; binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, FDR on the left). The grey top bar is the share of each condition's studies from oral sites.

### Periodontitis genera enriched in other conditions

*Is the genus reported more often in this condition than in others?* Cells: share of the condition's studies with the genus; outlined = enriched at FDR < 0.05 (Fisher's exact test). First column: all of BugSigDB.

```{r bsdb-conditions-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most often increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and their share of BugSigDB signatures of taxa increased in other conditions. See the text above for how to read the figure."
condition_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-conditions-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most often decreased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and their share of BugSigDB signatures of taxa decreased in other conditions. See the text above for how to read the figure."
condition_heatmap("decreased")
```

**Shows:** colorectal cancer is enriched for *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium*. Oral conditions (rheumatoid arthritis, oral cancers, smoking) look enriched, but not once body site is accounted for (next section). Decreased genera: only *Gemella* in smoking.

### Enrichment compared with conditions from the same body sites

As above, but each condition is compared only with studies from the same body site group (oral, gastrointestinal, other, mixed; stratified exact test), since oral genera are common in any oral sample.

```{r bsdb-site-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "As the previous enrichment heatmap (taxa increased in periodontitis), but each condition is compared with other conditions' signatures from the same body site group."
condition_heatmap("increased", match_site = TRUE)
```

```{r bsdb-site-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "As the previous enrichment heatmap (taxa decreased in periodontitis), but each condition is compared with other conditions' signatures from the same body site group."
condition_heatmap("decreased", match_site = TRUE)
```

**Shows:** only colorectal cancer remains, with the same four genera. The oral conditions' enrichment was a body site effect.

### Direction of periodontitis genera within each condition

*When the condition reports the genus, is it in the same direction as in periodontitis?* Colour: share of reports in the same direction; outlined = FDR < 0.05 (binomial test); grey = only 1–2 studies.

```{r bsdb-direction-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most consistently increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and how consistently they are reported as increased within other BugSigDB conditions."
direction_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-direction-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most consistently decreased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and how consistently they are reported as decreased within other BugSigDB conditions."
direction_heatmap("decreased")
```

**Shows:** only colorectal cancer is significant: *Peptostreptococcus* (27/27 studies increased), *Parvimonas* (24/24), *Porphyromonas* (22/23), *Fusobacterium* (32/37). No condition is significant for decreased genera.

### Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis

```{r bsdb-semantic-load}
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R (takes ~20 minutes)
semsim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")
```

Compares whole signatures at the reported rank (mostly species), without collapsing to genus.

- **PerioSigDB consensus:** taxa significantly more often increased (`r length(semsim$consensus$increased)`) or decreased (`r length(semsim$consensus$decreased)`) in periodontitis (binomial test).
- **Similarity:** semantic similarity on the NCBI taxonomy (best-match average of Lin similarity, as in BugSigDB's tools), for BugSigDB signatures with at least 5 taxa (smaller ones give extreme scores), ranked against BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (0.5 = typical): first against all of them, then only against those from the same body site group.
- **Test:** is a condition more similar than typical? One-sided Wilcoxon test. Rows are the 5 conditions most significantly similar to each periodontitis signature in the same direction, with every study unit.

```{r bsdb-semantic-c}
# similarity ranks among BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (and body site group if match_site)
similarity_ranks <- function(match_site = TRUE) {
  units <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
    # signatures with at least 5 taxa (as in the BugSigDB paper): smaller ones give extreme, noisy similarities
    filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
    inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
    summarise(up = mean(sim_increased), down = mean(sim_decreased),
              .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
    mutate(up = (rank(up) - 0.5) / n(), down = (rank(down) - 0.5) / n(),
           .by = all_of(if (match_site) c("direction", "site_group") else "direction")) |>
    filter(n() >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
    pivot_longer(c(up, down), names_to = "perio", values_to = "rank") |>
    mutate(perio = ifelse(perio == "up", "increased", "decreased"))

  # one-sided: more similar than typical, within each BugSigDB direction x periodontitis signature
  stats <- units |>
    summarise(
      studies = n(),
      mean_rank = mean(rank),
      ci = 1.96 * sd(rank) / sqrt(n()),
      p = wilcox.test(rank, mu = 0.5, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)$p.value,
      .by = c(Condition, direction, perio)
    ) |>
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(direction, perio))

  list(units = units, stats = stats)
}

semsim_site <- similarity_ranks()
semsim_all <- similarity_ranks(match_site = FALSE)

similarity_plot <- function(res, perio_dir, dir) {
  shown <- res$stats |>
    filter(perio == perio_dir, direction == dir) |>
    slice_min(p, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(label = paste0(Condition, " (", studies, ")\np = ", signif(p, 2), ", FDR = ", signif(fdr, 2)),
           label = fct_reorder(label, -p))
  points <- inner_join(res$units, select(shown, Condition, direction, perio, label),
                       by = c("Condition", "direction", "perio"))

  ggplot(shown, aes(y = label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_quasirandom(data = points, aes(x = rank), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, size = 1.1,
                     color = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6")[[perio_dir]], alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey10") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = fdr < 0.05), shape = 21, size = 3.5, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Periodontitis %s vs BugSigDB %s", perio_dir, dir),
         subtitle = if (dir == perio_dir) "Same direction" else "Opposite direction",
         x = sprintf("Similarity to periodontitis-%s signature (rank; 0.5 = typical)", perio_dir), y = NULL) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey35"))
}

# one grid: conditions as rows (shared), the four comparisons as columns
comparison_levels <- c("Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB increased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB decreased",
                       "Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB decreased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB increased")

similarity_grid <- function(res, n_top = 5) {
  label_comparison <- function(d) {
    d |> mutate(
      comparison = factor(sprintf("Perio %s\nvs BugSigDB %s", perio, direction), levels = comparison_levels),
      opposite = perio != direction
    )
  }
  # union of the n_top conditions most similar to each periodontitis signature (same direction),
  # ordered by their smallest p in those two comparisons
  conditions <- res$stats |>
    filter(perio == direction) |>
    slice_min(p, n = n_top, by = perio, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    summarise(best = min(p), .by = Condition) |>
    arrange(desc(best)) |>
    pull(Condition)

  stats <- res$stats |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions) |>
    label_comparison() |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = conditions),
           significance = case_when(fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05", p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05", .default = "Not significant") |>
             factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05", "Not significant")))
  units <- res$units |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions) |>
    label_comparison() |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = conditions))
  shade <- distinct(stats, comparison, opposite) |> filter(opposite)

  ggplot(stats, aes(y = Condition)) +
    geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "grey95") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_quasirandom(data = units, aes(x = rank, color = perio), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, size = 0.8,
                     alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), height = 0, linewidth = 0.7, color = "grey10") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = significance), shape = 21, size = 3, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "grey10", "p < 0.05" = "grey60", "Not significant" = "white"),
                      name = "Mean", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    facet_grid(. ~ comparison) +
    labs(x = "Similarity (rank among BugSigDB signatures; 0.5 = typical)", y = NULL,
         caption = "White columns: same direction as periodontitis; shaded columns: opposite direction") +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top",
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "lines"))
}
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-all-fig}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Which BugSigDB conditions resemble the periodontitis signatures? Columns: similarity to the periodontitis-increased (orange points) or -decreased (blue points) consensus, for BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (white) or the opposite direction (shaded). Similarity is ranked among all BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (0.5 = typical). Rows: the 5 conditions most significantly similar to each periodontitis signature (first two columns). Small points: study units; large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval."
similarity_grid(semsim_all)
```

**Shows:** colorectal cancer's increased taxa resemble the periodontitis-increased taxa (FDR = 0.0001), the only result passing FDR. Nominally, increased signatures of gastric cancer, HIV infection and chronic constipation resemble the periodontitis-increased taxa, and decreased signatures of smoking (p = 0.008), dry eye syndrome and COVID-19 resemble the periodontitis-decreased taxa (loss of oral commensals).

#### Compared with signatures from the same body sites

As above, but each signature is ranked only against BugSigDB signatures of the same direction and body site group, so oral conditions are compared with oral ones.

```{r bsdb-semantic-c-fig}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "As the previous figure, but similarity is ranked among BugSigDB signatures of the same direction and body site group."
similarity_grid(semsim_site)
```

**Shows:** colorectal cancer remains (FDR = 0.0003) while smoking drops out, as in the site-matched enrichment. Gastric cancer's increased signatures resemble both periodontitis signatures (nominally), i.e. oral taxa in general.

### Taxa shared by periodontitis and colorectal cancer

Colorectal cancer's increased consensus, built as for PerioSigDB (binomial test across its studies), against the periodontitis-increased consensus. Cells: Lin similarity (1 = same taxon, outlined; about 0.9 = same genus).

```{r bsdb-crc-consensus}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Lin similarity between the taxa increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB consensus, rows) and in colorectal cancer (consensus, columns). Outlined: the same taxon."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.R
taxon_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.rds")

terminal_id <- function(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", unique(sub("^.*[|]", "", x)))

perio_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(semsim$consensus),
  perio_direction = rep(names(semsim$consensus), lengths(semsim$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(semsim$taxon_tests, id = ids, perio_up = increased, perio_down = decreased), by = "id") |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", taxon_sim$names[id], perio_up, perio_down))

crc_consensus <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(Condition == "Colorectal cancer") |>
  mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
  unnest(taxon) |>
  distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    n = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")
  ) |>
  filter(p < 0.05, taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim)) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", sub(" <[^>]+>", "", taxon_sim$names[taxon]), increased, decreased))

perio_up <- filter(perio_consensus, perio_direction == "increased")
crc_up <- filter(crc_consensus, direction == "increased")

tidyr::expand_grid(select(perio_up, id, row = label), select(crc_up, taxon, col = label)) |>
  mutate(
    sim = taxon_sim$sim[cbind(taxon, id)],
    row = factor(row, levels = rev(perio_up$label[order(taxon_sim$lineage[perio_up$id])])),
    col = factor(col, levels = crc_up$label[order(taxon_sim$lineage[crc_up$taxon])])
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = col, y = row, fill = sim)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, sim > 0.999), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.9, fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f3f1", high = "#c0392b", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Lin\nsimilarity") +
  labs(x = "Increased in colorectal cancer (consensus)", y = "Increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB consensus)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 50, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Five taxa are shared exactly (*P. intermedia*, *F. nucleatum*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *P. stomatis*, *P. micra*) and several more are close relatives; *Treponema*, *Tannerella*, *Fretibacterium* and *Desulfobulbus* have no close counterpart. (The colorectal cancer decreased consensus, *Faecalibacterium*, is unrelated to periodontitis.)

### Agreement across approaches

Every approach singles out colorectal cancer, and only colorectal cancer, after FDR correction. Site-matched enrichment is the fairest genus-level test, the direction test confirms the genera move as in periodontitis, and whole-signature similarity confirms it at species level. Apparent links to oral conditions disappear once body site is accounted for.

### Suggestive results (not significant)

Picked after looking at several hundred tests, so hypotheses only:

- **Gastric cancer:** *Fusobacterium* in nearly half of studies, almost always increased.
- **Rheumatoid arthritis:** *Treponema* and *Selenomonas* enriched and increased.
- **Smoking:** loss of oral commensals (*Gemella*, *Corynebacterium*, *Granulicatella*) with more *Fusobacterium*.
- **Across many conditions:** *Fusobacterium*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Parvimonas* tend to be increased and *Haemophilus* and *Neisseria* decreased, suggesting part of the periodontitis signature is a generic dysbiosis pattern.

**Caveats:** studies are treated as independent; the disease-vs-control filter works on group names; aggregating PerioSigDB species to genus loses specificity (e.g. *P. gingivalis* up, *P. catoniae* down).

# Summary of options

```{r summary-table}
tribble(
  ~Option, ~Question, ~Form, ~Notes,
  "1. Completeness heatmap", "What metadata are available?", "Heatmap (fields × studies)", "Good supplementary figure; frames all others",
  "2. Paired comparison", "How do health and periodontitis groups differ?", "Paired slopes, small multiples", "Recommended main figure",
  "3. Severity by classification", "Is 'periodontitis' comparable across studies?", "Beeswarm, small multiples", "Recommended for within-periodontitis variation",
  "4. Trends over time", "Have cohorts changed over time?", "Scatter + trend", "Year confounded with method",
  "5. Classification", "How was periodontitis defined?", "Stacked bars + count tile", "Context for stratification",
  "6. Systemic condition", "Are comorbid populations included?", "Bar chart", "Half not recorded yet",
  "7. Methods and resolution", "How do PerioSigDB and BugSigDB differ structurally?", "Stacked bars", "Explains species vs genus mismatch",
  "8. Metadata fields", "What does each database record?", "Dot matrix", "Shows complementary fields and gaps",
  "9. Taxa across conditions", "Where do periodontitis-linked genera appear elsewhere?", "Genus heatmaps, similarity dot plots, colorectal cancer heatmap", "Most novel; site-matched enrichment most defensible"
) |>
  kbl(caption = "Candidate figures and tables.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE)
```

**Suggested combination:**

- **Main text:** Option 2 (paired comparison), plus Option 3 (severity by classification).
- **Supplement:** Option 1 (completeness).
- **Positioning against BugSigDB:** Option 8 (complementary metadata) and Option 9 (taxa across conditions).
